description: The CAST is a questionnaire in which a parent or carer of a primary-school-age child answers questions about social interaction, communication, play and interests. It was developed in the UK to help identify children who may have autistic traits and might benefit from a fuller assessment by a specialist.

form_name: Screen for Child Anxiety Related Disorders (SCARED) Parent Version
description: The SCARED asks about the different ways anxiety can show up in children: panic-type physical feelings, general worrying, fear of being apart from parents, shyness or worry around other people, and worries about school. It has 41 questions and takes about 10 minutes.
attribution: SCARED © Birmaher et al. Used with permission.

form_name: Vanderbilt ADHD Diagnostic Parent Rating Scale (VADPRS)
description: The Vanderbilt is a widely used questionnaire in which a parent or carer describes the attention, activity and behaviour they see in their child at home. It covers the core features of ADHD (difficulty focusing, being very active or impulsive), as well as mood, worries and how the child is getting on with schoolwork and friendships, giving a rounded picture rather than a single score.
attribution: Copyright ©2002 American Academy of Pediatrics and National Initiative for Children's Healthcare Quality. Adapted from the Vanderbilt Rating Scales developed by Mark L. Wolraich, MD.

form_name: SWAN (Strengths and Weaknesses of ADHD-symptoms and Normal-behaviour)
description: The SWAN is a questionnaire in which a parent or carer rates their child's attention and activity across the full range, from far below average to far above average, compared with other children of the same age. Unlike questionnaires that only ask how often a problem happens, it captures strengths as well as challenges, giving a fairer picture.
attribution: The SWAN Rating Scale. James M. Swanson, Ph.D., University of California, Irvine.

description: The GAD-7 is a short questionnaire in which an adult describes how much worry and anxiety they have experienced over the last two weeks, such as feeling nervous or on edge, being unable to stop worrying, trouble relaxing, restlessness and irritability.

The AQ-Child is a parent-completed version of the Autism Spectrum Quotient for children aged 4–11. Its 50 statements cover social skills, communication, attention to detail, attention switching and imagination. A higher score reflects more autism-associated traits. It has 50 questions and takes about 8 minutes.

form_name: Q-CHAT (Quantitative Checklist for Autism in Toddlers)
description: The Q-CHAT is a questionnaire for parents of toddlers (roughly 18–30 months) about early social communication, play and behaviour. It gives a score along a range rather than a yes/no result. A higher score reflects more autism-related features parents are noticing at this early age. It has 25 questions and takes about 5–10 minutes.
